title: Secrets and generated keys live in SSM Parameter Store SecureString, created by infrastructure code
description:
Owner rule (2026-10-21): secrets and config live in SSM Parameter Store standard SecureString (free, default aws/ssm key); Secrets Manager (0.40 USD per secret per month) only where a service definitely requires it; nothing manually configured, so generated values need an infrastructure-as-code creator.

VERIFIED INVENTORY (2026-10-21, names only). chatticus-production account, 11 secrets: InvokeKey and OperatorKey one pair per environment (stacks ChatticusThinTurn{Development,Staging,Production}, by design: each environment has its own front door), ModelGatewaySigningKey one (ChatticusControlPlaneDevelopment only, created under isDevelopment; staging and production have no owner path), IntakeOriginKey one (stack ChatticusMarketing, private repo AnthusAI/Chattic.us-web, infra/lib/marketing-stack.ts), chatticus/{development,staging,production}/oauth/google three (created by hand, imported by name with Secret.fromSecretNameV2 in infra/lib/auth-stack.ts). Old staging account: 3 (OperatorKey, InvokeKey, oauth/google): true orphans, no Chatticus stack exists there any more (CDK RETAIN left them). Legacy account: 7 Chatticus secrets (3 InvokeKey, 1 OperatorKey, 3 oauth/google) owned by still-existing but stale stacks (ChatticusThinTurn, ThinTurnStaging, ThinTurnProduction, last updated Aug 30-31; Auth stacks for the oauth ones) -- stale, not referenced by anything in the new accounts. The three production-account InvokeKey are not duplicates; the old-account copies are.

WHY SOME MUST STAY IN SECRETS MANAGER (verified in the CloudFormation docs, dynamic-references-ssm-secure-strings): ssm-secure dynamic references work only for a short list (Directory Service passwords, ElastiCache AuthToken, IAM LoginProfile, Firehose Redshift, OpsWorks, RDS and Redshift master passwords) and not in custom resources. Not supported: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolIdentityProvider ProviderDetails client_secret (auth-stack.ts passes the Google secret through SecretValue from Secrets Manager), CloudFront origin custom headers (invoke key, web-stack.ts unsafeUnwrap into X-Chatticus-Invoke-Key), Lambda environment values at deploy (IntakeOriginKey). Secrets Manager dynamic references work everywhere. So: invoke key x3, IntakeOriginKey, Google OAuth x3 = 7 secrets STAY. Runtime-only secrets MOVE: OperatorKey x3, ModelGatewaySigningKey x1 = 4 secrets. Possible later removal of the invoke key: CloudFront Origin Access Control to the Function URL (AWS_IAM) needs a spike because POST bodies need a payload hash header and the front door streams responses.

TARGET NAMES: /chatticus/<env>/thin-turn/operator-key, /chatticus/development/model-gateway/signing-key (SecureString, Standard tier, alias/aws/ssm, tags chatticus:environment and aws stack tags).

IAC CREATOR (new construct GeneratedSecureString in infra/lib): a Provider-framework custom resource with a small Node Lambda. Create: generate with crypto.randomBytes (base64url, no punctuation, length per input), PutParameter Type SecureString Tier Standard Overwrite false; if ParameterAlreadyExists adopt it unchanged (this is the migration seam). Update: no-op. Delete: no-op (parameters are RETAIN, like the existing secrets). Response data carries only the parameter name and version, never the value; Provider isCompleteHandler not needed; the handler never logs the event or the value. Do not use AwsCustomResource (its parameters would put the value in the template) and do not use ssm-secure dynamic references (unsupported in custom resources). Handler role: ssm:PutParameter on the exact parameter ARN only; with the AWS-managed aws/ssm key no kms grant is needed because the key policy allows principals authorized for SSM in the account (the existing /chatticus/<env>/thin-turn/openai-api-key SecureString is already read this way with ssm:GetParameter only, no kms statement).

RUNTIME: consumers call ssm GetParameter WithDecryption on the exact ARN. Front door reads the operator key once per composition (cold start) as today; signing key readers (FrontDoor, ComputerStarter, OwnerCredentialBroker, 15 s cache) keep their caching. Env var changes from *_SECRET_ARN to *_PARAMETER_NAME; IAM changes from secretsmanager:GetSecretValue to ssm:GetParameter on the exact ARN. SSM standard throughput 40 TPS default: ample for one household.

INTERACTIONS: role-access manifest and IAM simulator (conversation/src/gateway/role-access-manifest.json, bin/simulate-role-access.ts) currently cover no secrets; add negative rows so the owner supervisor and per-turn roles are denied ssm:GetParameter on the signing key and operator key parameters. infra/test thin-turn, control-plane, computer-owner and rotate-invoke-key tests, features/invoke_key_rotation.feature (invoke key unchanged). docs/OWNER_CREDENTIAL_REVOCATION.md sections 0, 1.1, 2.1 (operator bearer read), 5 (signing key rotation), 6 (operator key): replace secretsmanager commands with ssm put-parameter --overwrite and get-parameter commands that never print; chatticus-541dc7 (signing key rotation story) must be updated to the SSM semantics. Caveat for revocation: SSM keeps up to 100 versions (history) readable by anyone with ssm:GetParameterHistory or name:version; after a leak rotate AND deny GetParameterHistory, or delete and recreate the parameter (the IaC creator re-creates it on the next deploy only if the custom resource is replaced; document the exact steps). SSM has no AWSPREVIOUS stage, so the operator and signing keys have no overlap window (signing key already had none; operator key is human-only).

MIGRATION WITHOUT DOWNTIME: operator key and signing key both rotate harmlessly instead of being copied, because no running system holds them: operator key is used only by an operator by hand (blast radius: nothing); the signing key exists in development only, and a rotation stops every running owner and fails turns in flight (no customers there, already the documented last-resort cost). So the IaC creator generates fresh values and nobody reads or copies an existing value. If the owner prefers continuity for the signing key, a one-off owner-run script piping aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --query SecretString --output text into aws ssm put-parameter --type SecureString --overwrite via a file descriptor, run BEFORE the deploy so the creator adopts it, never printed. Invoke keys are not migrated.

ORDER (a wrong order can lock out the front door or the operator): 1) land the construct and tests, no consumer change. 2) Deploy thin-turn per environment (development first): new SSM operator-key parameter created, old secret and its secret-arn SSM parameter and outputs stay. 3) Deploy control-plane: FrontDoor reads the parameter; confirm acceptance (invoke key unaffected). 4) Remove the old secret construct in a LATER deploy; HAZARD: ModelGatewaySigningKey has removalPolicy DESTROY (scheduled deletion), and thin-turn operator secret outputs carry exportName values that a consuming stack could still import (check cloudformation list-imports first); HAZARD: the thin-turn deploy must precede the control-plane deploy because control-plane resolves the parameter name from SSM at synth. 5) Signing key: development only, rotate after the control-plane deploy and restart owners. Never do the old-secret removal and the consumer switch in one deploy (rollback would point at a deleted secret, and the Secrets Manager scheduled-deletion window is the only safety net). Do not touch InvokeKey: the Web stack deploy script pins its version id (-c invokeKeyVersionId) and rotate-invoke-key.sh depends on the AWSCURRENT/AWSPREVIOUS stages.

COST: Secrets Manager 0.40 USD per secret per month plus 0.05 USD per 10,000 API calls. Moving 4 secrets saves 1.60 USD per month; deleting the 10 orphaned Chatticus secrets (3 old staging, 7 legacy) saves 4.00 USD per month (needs owner approval and, in legacy, retiring stale stacks); total about 5.60 USD per month of about 8.40 USD today. Small money; the real win is that generated keys become IaC-owned and consistent. SSM standard SecureString with aws/ssm: no parameter charge, no key charge (KMS request charges negligible).

OTHER MANUAL ITEMS FOUND (not part of this story, owner decision): the three Google OAuth secrets and the three openai-api-key SecureStrings are created by hand (vendor-issued values; IaC can create an empty shell and the owner puts the value once, but a vendor-issued value is inherently manual).

Sub-tasks cover each secret group.
